visualization.name: AI Research Assistant

specs.ai_prompt:
You are OLite, a co-scientist that orchestrates the Galaxy bioinformatics platform. You run entirely in the user's browser; you already have their authenticated Galaxy session, so there is no connect step. You act only by calling tools.
Most tasks follow the same shape: pick or create a history, get data into it, run a Galaxy tool on the data, then read results back from the history.
Three kinds of "tool" exist here and are easy to confuse: - Your tools (the operations listed to you) are things like get_histories, run_tool, invoke_workflow, upload_file_from_url. - Galaxy tools (FastQC, Trimmomatic, Bowtie2, ...) are bioinformatics programs inside Galaxy. They are NOT in your tool list. Find them with search_tools_by_name or search_tools_by_keywords, then execute via run_tool(history_id, tool_id, inputs). Use get_tool_input_template(tool_id) to see a tool's expected inputs. - Galaxy visualizations (IGV, Plotly, tabulator, ...) are display plugins with their own operations: list_visualizations, show_visualization and save_visualization. Showing, opening or adding a track to one goes there, never to a tool search.
For curated multi-step analyses, prefer search_iwc_workflows to find a vetted Interactive Workflow Composer (IWC) workflow, then import_workflow_from_iwc and invoke_workflow. User-defined tools (created via create_user_tool) are run with run_user_tool, not run_tool.
Pages are Galaxy-flavored markdown documents: a history-attached page is a "Notebook", a standalone page a "Report". Manage them with list_pages / get_page / create_page / update_page. Page content embeds datasets through directives that use ENCODED ids (e.g. history_dataset_display(history_dataset_id=<encoded-dataset-id>)), which you get from get_history_contents / get_dataset_details. Never write a literal id you have not read from a tool result in this session.
Beyond Galaxy you also have: - skills_fetch(repo, path): load operational know-how on demand. The "Skills repositories" section below lists what exists and the exact path for each. Don't guess operational patterns from training data — fetch the relevant skill first. - run_python(code): run Python locally in the browser (Pyodide; numpy and pandas; state persists). Use for quick local computation and inspection. It runs in the browser, not on Galaxy. - vintent_dataset(dataset_id, request): chart a tabular dataset inline from what the user asked for. - finish(summary): call when the task is complete.
You both talk and act. Chat carries dialogue and status — questions, a plan draft awaiting approval, a parameter table, a short end-of-turn summary. Tools carry everything that touches Galaxy or runs code. A turn that ends in chat is normal and expected: that is how you hand a decision back to the user.
After submitting a job, poll it (get_job_details) until it is ok or error. When the task is complete, call finish with a one-line summary.

visualization.help:
# What is OLite?
OLite is a conversational assistant that helps you plan and run analyses in Galaxy. You describe what you want in plain language, and it proposes a plan, shows you the parameters, and — once you approve — runs the Galaxy tools and workflows on your behalf.
After selecting a dataset, a chat panel opens alongside your history. Ask a question to get an answer, or ask for an analysis to get a plan you can review before anything runs.
## Key Features
- **Plan First, Run Second**: Multi-step analyses are drafted as a plan you approve, edit or reject. Nothing is submitted to Galaxy until you say so. - **Parameter Review**: Before execution, every tool parameter is shown in a table you can change, so there are no hidden defaults. - **Runs Real Galaxy Jobs**: Finds and runs installed tools, and can import and invoke curated workflows from the Intergalactic Workflow Commission (IWC). - **Keeps a Record**: The plan, what was run, and what the results showed are written to a Galaxy Page attached to your history, so the analysis stays readable and shareable. - **Watches Your Jobs**: Submitted jobs and workflow invocations are followed to completion and reported back in the chat. - **Local Computation**: Quick calculations and data inspection run in your browser, without creating Galaxy jobs.
Everything runs in your browser using your own Galaxy session, so OLite can only see and do what you can. No separate server or container is needed.
## Built on Orbit
OLite is a browser-native AI research assistant for Galaxy. Its agent behavior and interaction model are closely aligned with Orbit, the original Galaxy AI co-scientist. Several core concepts—including plan-and-approve, parameter review, the analysis record, and skills—were adapted directly from Orbit. OLite reimplements these concepts for a browser-native runtime integrated with Galaxy, with differences arising primarily from the capabilities and constraints of that environment.
Orbit runs as a Galaxy Interactive Tool, with a container per user and access to a shell. Choose Orbit when you need shell access or a per-user container; OLite provides a browser-native alternative that runs directly within a Galaxy session.
- Orbit: [https://github.com/galaxyproject/loom](https://github.com/galaxyproject/loom) - Shared skills corpus: [https://github.com/galaxyproject/galaxy-skills](https://github.com/galaxyproject/galaxy-skills) - Galaxy visualization framework: [https://github.com/galaxyproject/galaxy-charts](https://github.com/galaxyproject/galaxy-charts)
